adultGuide.title: Clipboard Story Paragraph Focus Adult Guide
bullets: Print the clipboard paragraph focus cards, blank paragraph frames, and guide pages before the adult-led paper session.
Begin with one fictional paragraph plan, then coach a main idea, two useful details, detail order, one linking sentence, one cut idea, and a final focused copy.
Keep every example made-up, broad, printable, offline, paper-only, and guided by an adult.
Use small paper slips so the writer can move details before copying the final paragraph.
Replace narrow real facts with invented names, broad story places, and pretend objects before writing begins.
End each activity by copying one focused fictional paragraph that keeps one main idea and two helpful details.

paragraphFocusRoutines.name: Main Idea Clip
paragraphFocusRoutines.bestFor: Choosing the one idea a fictional paragraph will stay about.
steps: The adult places one blank paragraph frame on the clipboard strip and writes the story topic: ____________________.
The writer states the one main idea the paragraph should prove or show: ____________________.
The adult asks which words in the main idea must guide every sentence: ____________________.
The writer copies the main idea line at the top of the paragraph frame: ____________________.

paragraphFocusRoutines.name: Detail Pair Sort
paragraphFocusRoutines.bestFor: Choosing two useful details and leaving out loose ideas.
steps: The adult writes four invented detail notes on small paper slips: ____________________.
The writer chooses two details that clearly support the main idea: ____________________.
The adult asks which other detail is interesting but belongs outside this paragraph: ____________________.
The writer places the detail pair under the main idea line: ____________________.

paragraphFocusRoutines.name: Detail Order Lineup
paragraphFocusRoutines.bestFor: Putting two useful details in the clearest order.
steps: The adult sets the two chosen details side by side below the main idea: ____________________.
The writer numbers the detail that should come first and the detail that should come second: ____________________.
The adult asks why that order will help the reader follow the pretend moment: ____________________.
The writer copies the ordered detail notes in the paragraph frame: ____________________.

paragraphFocusRoutines.name: Linking Sentence Bridge
paragraphFocusRoutines.bestFor: Adding one sentence that connects the main idea to the details.
steps: The adult points from the main idea to the first detail and asks for one linking sentence: ____________________.
The writer drafts a linking sentence that connects the main idea to detail one: ____________________.
The adult asks whether the sentence points back to the same paragraph focus: ____________________.
The writer writes the linking sentence before the two detail lines: ____________________.

paragraphFocusRoutines.name: Extra Idea Lift
paragraphFocusRoutines.bestFor: Cutting one interesting idea that pulls the paragraph away from its focus.
steps: The adult marks one sentence or note that wanders away from the main idea: ____________________.
The writer explains why that extra idea can wait for another paper page: ____________________.
The adult asks which word or detail should stay after the extra idea comes out: ____________________.
The writer rewrites the paragraph plan with the extra idea removed: ____________________.

paragraphFocusRoutines.name: Final Focus Copy
paragraphFocusRoutines.bestFor: Copying one focused fictional paragraph after the plan is clean.
steps: The adult reads the paragraph plan in order: main idea, linking sentence, detail one, detail two: ____________________.
The writer checks that every sentence supports the same focus: ____________________.
The adult asks if one word should move, change, or come out before final copying: ____________________.
The writer copies the final focused fictional paragraph on a fresh sheet: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Main Idea Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Write the one main idea this fictional paragraph will stay about: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask what every sentence should point back to: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Two Useful Details Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: List two useful invented details that support the main idea: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask which two details help the reader understand the same idea: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Detail Order Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Number the two details in the order the paragraph should use them: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask why the first detail should come before the second: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Linking Sentence Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Write one linking sentence between the main idea and the first detail: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask how the linking sentence keeps the paragraph focused: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Extra Idea Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Find one interesting extra idea that does not belong in this paragraph: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask where that idea could wait on another blank paper page: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Focus Check Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Check each sentence and mark yes if it supports the main idea: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask which sentence most clearly proves the paragraph focus: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Opening Line Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Turn the main idea into a clear opening line for one fictional paragraph: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask whether the opening line tells the reader what to expect: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Detail Pair Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Write the detail pair as two separate sentences that support one focus: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask whether both detail sentences belong under the same main idea: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Final Focus Copy Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Copy the final focused paragraph after one extra idea has been removed: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask what changed from the loose plan to the final paragraph: ____________________.

takeHomeParagraphSlips.title: Paragraph Polish Slip
takeHomeParagraphSlips.direction: Move, change, or remove one word so the final paragraph reads more smoothly: ____________________.
takeHomeParagraphSlips.familyLine: Ask which small change made the paragraph easier to follow: ____________________.
